theoryOfChange: The Chicago Community Bond Fund (CCBF) operates with a clear theory of change rooted in abolitionist principles and a commitment to grassroots organizing. A co-founder stated, "Because of our theory of change, our commitment to movement work, and our belief that grassroots organizing is what achieves social change, there was an agreement early on to have an expansive role, but also to prioritize those sorts of political arrests, to prioritize support for grassroots social movement." CCBF explicitly states its belief in the “invest/divest” framework from the Movement for Black Lives, aiming to divest from jails, prisons, and policing while investing in impacted communities. Their work extends beyond paying bonds to include public education about the criminal legal system and advocating for the abolition of money bond. The organization is committed to long-term relationship building and organizing with people directly impacted by criminalization and policing. Their advocacy efforts, detailed on their website, include working on legislation and lawsuits to end money bond and pretrial incarceration in Illinois, often in collaboration with organizations like the Coalition to End Money Bond. This multi-faceted approach demonstrates a strategic framework for achieving systemic change.
